confidence_note: Multiple omic layers support degradative capacity and activity, but do not quantify a whole-fjord remineralization flux.

subject: habitat:active-layer-soil
statement: Bayelva active-layer microbial genomes and transcripts encode broad carbohydrate-degradation pathways that provide a terrestrial functional baseline for comparison with Svalbard fjord sediments.
scope: March 2021 active-layer cores from Bayelva near Ny-Alesund, represented by 44 recovered MAGs and community-level omics.
evidence_basis: Genome-resolved metagenomics, transcriptomics, and carbohydrate-active-enzyme annotation.
locator: Results: community composition and carbohydrate metabolism in active-layer soils
confidence_note: The molecular data support functional potential and expression, not an in situ seasonal carbon-turnover rate.

subject: driver:permafrost-thaw
statement: H2-18O quantitative stable-isotope probing resolved distinct early and late microbial growers after active-layer soil thaw, with only 22% of labeled sequence variants growing at both 21 and 98 days.
scope: Replicated microcosms derived from one 18-27-centimetre interval of a frozen Bayelva soil core and incubated at 4 degrees Celsius.
evidence_basis: Density-resolved incorporation of oxygen-18 into newly synthesized DNA at two incubation endpoints.
locator: Results: early and late communities; taxon-specific growth following thaw
confidence_note: The isotope signal directly identifies growth in the experiment, while generalization beyond the single core is limited.

subject: process:microbial-predation
statement: Growth after thaw included Myxococcota, Patescibacteria, and Bdellovibrionota affiliated with predatory or epibiotic lifestyles, indicating that cell-cell interactions contribute to post-thaw turnover.
scope: Bayelva active-layer microcosms at 21 and 98 days; ecological lifestyles are assigned from taxonomy and prior knowledge.
evidence_basis: Oxygen-18 labeling of sequence variants taxonomically associated with predation or obligate epibiosis.
locator: Results: Epibiont and predatory phyla
confidence_note: Growth is directly detected, but actual prey or host pairs were not measured in the microcosms.

subject: taxon:h5n1-clade-2344b
statement: Highly pathogenic H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b genotype B3.2 was confirmed in all three sampled Tristan skua carcasses from Gough Island, and two samples yielded viral whole-genome sequences.
scope: Three carcasses sampled on Gough Island on 20 September 2024 according to Table 1 and strain identifiers.
evidence_basis: H5-specific RT-PCR, brain and oropharyngeal testing, virus isolation, and whole-genome sequencing.
locator: Results: Diagnostic evaluation of samples; Table 1
confidence_note: Infection is laboratory confirmed, although the sample is too small to estimate population prevalence or mortality.

subject: process:seabird-migration
statement: Phylogenetic source-sink reconstruction and skua tracking support a plausible South Georgia-to-Gough H5N1 dispersal pathway, but do not directly observe movement by an infected bird.
scope: Two Gough viral genomes compared with Antarctic and sub-Antarctic sequences, plus annual light-level tracks from eight Tristan skuas collected in earlier years.
evidence_basis: Viral phylogeny, asymmetric geographic transition modeling, and independent seabird movement tracks.
locator: Results: phylogenetic analysis and ringing and tracking data; Figs. 2-4
confidence_note: Genomic relatedness and ecological connectivity align, but the timing and individual transmission route are unobserved.

subject: src:cao-2026-jonahs-icefish-genome
statement: The Jonah's icefish reference resource contains a 1.27-gigabase assembly with 96.8% of sequence anchored to 24 chromosomes, a scaffold N50 of 51.82 megabases, and 31,777 predicted protein-coding genes.
scope: One adult specimen collected in Prydz Bay in January 2024 and sequenced with Illumina, PacBio HiFi, Iso-Seq, and Hi-C methods.
evidence_basis: Chromosome-scale assembly, Hi-C anchoring, integrated gene annotation, and assembly-quality validation.
locator: Abstract; Methods: de novo assembly and gene prediction; Data Records; Technical Validation
confidence_note: Assembly metrics are directly reported and supported by mapping and BUSCO checks, but the resource represents one individual.

subject: taxon:mpov-44t-a
statement: MpoV-44T.A and MpoV-44T.B are independently replicating lytic dsDNA viruses of Micromonas polaris, but they differ substantially in genome sequence, host range, infectivity, and lysis timing.
scope: Viruses separated from a Kongsfjorden-derived mixed culture and tested mainly on Micromonas polaris RCC2258 under controlled nutrient-replete conditions.
evidence_basis: Virus separation, complete genome sequencing, host-range assays, flow cytometry, qPCR, and single-virus infections.
locator: Results 3.1-3.2; Figs. 1-3; Supplementary Tables S1-S2
confidence_note: Independent infection is experimentally demonstrated for the cultured system, while natural host range remains less constrained.

subject: taxon:mpov-44t-a
statement: When equal particle numbers of both viruses were added to the shared host, MpoV-44T.B genome production reached only 18 plus or minus 8% of its single-infection production, whereas MpoV-44T.A production was not significantly reduced.
scope: Triplicate dual-infection cultures of Micromonas polaris RCC2258 with a target virus-to-host ratio of 10:1 for each virus.
evidence_basis: Strain-specific qPCR and flow-cytometric host and virus time series in single and dual infections.
locator: Results 3.3: Coexistence; Fig. 5c-d
confidence_note: Suppression is directly measured in the laboratory treatment, but the responsible molecular mechanism was not identified.

subject: habitat:marine-water-column
statement: MpoV-44T.B-like reads were consistently more abundant than MpoV-44T.A-like reads in the analyzed Tara Arctic metagenomes, reversing the competitive ordering seen in the nutrient-replete dual-infection experiment.
scope: Fourteen surface and deep-chlorophyll-maximum samples from seven Tara Oceans Polar Circle stations collected May-September 2013.
evidence_basis: Kraken2 classification of environmental metagenomic reads against the two isolate genomes and paired station-level comparison.
locator: Results 3.4; Fig. 6
confidence_note: The relative read signal is statistically consistent across the dataset but depends on classifier specificity and does not establish absolute particle abundance.

subject: habitat:fur-seal-gut
statement: All four Antarctic fur-seal fecal metagenomes contained chitin-degradation genes, and MAGs assigned complementary hydrolytic steps to different bacterial taxa, consistent with cross-feeding on a krill-rich diet.
scope: Fresh feces from four individuals sampled within one kilometre on the Fildes Peninsula, King George Island.
evidence_basis: Shotgun metagenomic CAZy annotation, genome-resolved binning, and microscopic identification of krill exoskeletal remains.
locator: Results: Genetic analysis related to chitin degradation; Fig. 5
confidence_note: Pathway complementarity is supported by gene annotations but was not tested with substrate turnover or expression measurements.

subject: habitat:fur-seal-gut
statement: The four fecal metagenomes contained 16 annotated antimicrobial-resistance gene types, including bacitracin, polymyxin, and multidrug categories, but these sequences do not establish phenotypic resistance or anthropogenic selection.
scope: Four Antarctic fur seals from one King George Island sampling campaign; resistance genes normalized and annotated from metagenomic sequence data.
evidence_basis: CARD and ARGs-OAP sequence annotation without culture-based susceptibility testing.
locator: Results: relative abundance and composition of antibiotic resistance genes; Discussion; Fig. 7
confidence_note: Gene presence is supported, while phenotype, source, transferability, and clinical risk remain untested.

subject: habitat:sea-ice
statement: Bulk metagenomes from nine Arctic, Baltic, and Antarctic sea-ice samples yielded 550 vOTUs, with 528 of 537 classified vOTUs assigned to Caudoviricetes.
scope: Three samples from each of Arctic early-summer 2015, Baltic winter 2006, and Weddell-Gyre winter 2013 sea ice.
evidence_basis: geNomad viral-contig detection, CheckV quality screening, 95% ANI/85% alignment-fraction dereplication, and sequence-based taxonomy.
locator: Results: Diversity and taxonomy of sea ice viruses; Fig. 3
confidence_note: The catalogue is reproducible for these metagenomes, but bulk membrane-filter sequencing under-recovers small free viral particles and most genomes were incomplete.

subject: taxon:caudoviricetes
statement: Hosts were computationally assigned to 187 sea-ice vOTUs, with Gammaproteobacteria and Bacteroidia the most frequent predicted host classes.
scope: The 550-vOTU Arctic, Baltic, and Antarctic sea-ice catalogue.
evidence_basis: iPHoP host prediction at genus- and family-level score thresholds, not isolate infection tests.
locator: Results: Predicted hosts of the sea ice vOTUs; Fig. 5
confidence_note: Only 187 of 550 vOTUs received a prediction and no host association was experimentally validated.

subject: habitat:sea-ice
statement: Austral-winter Southern Ocean sea ice contained 24–115 nanomolar total DMSP, 2–38 times the concentrations measured in contemporaneous seawater samples.
scope: Six ice sections and 18 seawater samples from the July 2022 SCALE cruise.
evidence_basis: Acid-preserved DMSP samples measured as headspace DMS after alkaline hydrolysis by purge-and-trap gas chromatography.
locator: Results: DMSP standing stock concentrations; Fig. 2B-C
confidence_note: The concentration contrast is directly measured but represents one winter cruise and three ice cores.

subject: taxon:ice-algae
statement: DSYB- and DSYE-bearing eukaryotic algae were predicted to dominate DMSP biosynthetic potential, while bacterial producers and abundant dmdA, dddD, and dddK genes expanded the inferred producer–consumer network.
scope: Greater-than-3-micrometre and 0.2–3-micrometre fractions from Southern Ocean winter sea ice and seawater.
evidence_basis: Metagenomic taxonomic assignment and normalized homolog detection for known DMSP biosynthesis and catabolism genes.
locator: Results: Algal DMSP production; bacterial DMSP production and catabolism; Fig. 3
confidence_note: Gene presence supports metabolic potential but not expression, compound-specific turnover, or organism-resolved rates.

subject: process:turbulent-nutrient-supply
statement: The estimated turbulent silicic-acid flux across the ice–ocean interface was similar in magnitude to the silicon demand inferred for the observed ice-algal bloom.
scope: One early-spring West Greenland landfast-ice site adjacent to marine-terminating glaciers.
evidence_basis: Turbulence-controlled molecular-sublayer flux calculation compared with production-derived Redfield–Brzezinski silicon demand.
locator: Results: nutrient flux and biotic parameters; Discussion
confidence_note: Agreement in magnitudes supports the mechanism, but the flux and limitation were not experimentally manipulated.

subject: habitat:bottom-sea-ice
statement: A Nitzschia-frigida-rich bottom-ice bloom fixed 146 ± 4.8 milligrams carbon per square metre per day and accumulated 42.4 ± 1.6 milligrams chlorophyll a per square metre.
scope: One early-spring sampling event near marine-terminating glaciers in West Greenland.
evidence_basis: Primary-production incubation, chlorophyll measurement, and qualitative microscopy.
locator: Results: Biotic parameters; Fig. 3
confidence_note: The values are directly measured for one site and date but should not be spatially or annually extrapolated.

subject: driver:environmental-filtering
statement: Glacial bacterial lineages dominated foreland MAGs but were rare in fjord MAGs, indicating strong filtering between the glacier–foreland system and coastal seawater.
scope: Thirty-two metagenomes along the Ny-Ålesund glacier–foreland–Kongsfjorden continuum.
evidence_basis: Abundance and habitat overlap of 309 reconstructed species-level bacterial MAGs.
locator: Results and Discussion: bacterial community composition, diversity, and microbial source tracking; Figs. 2-3
confidence_note: The habitat partition is strong for recovered MAGs, but establishment, viability, and immigration rates were not measured.

subject: habitat:glacier-foreland
statement: Genome-resolved pathway profiles separated carbon-fixation potential concentrated in glacial MAGs, a foreland denitrification hotspot, and sulfur-oxidation potential dominant in the fjord.
scope: Glacial, foreland, and fjord MAGs recovered near Ny-Ålesund, Svalbard.
evidence_basis: Metabolic annotation of 309 bacterial MAGs and comparison of pathway distributions among habitats.
locator: Results and Discussion: metabolic profiles across the glacier-to-fjord continuum
confidence_note: The genome content establishes potential, not pathway expression or process rates.

subject: habitat:sea-ice
statement: The Amundsen sea-ice zone showed selective total-iron enrichment relative to offshore waters without comparable enrichment of the other measured metals, a pattern consistent with sea-ice melt supplying iron.
scope: Surface-water stations classified as Amundsen Sea Polynya, sea-ice zone, and oceanic area.
evidence_basis: Regional comparison of dissolved, labile particulate, and refractory particulate trace-metal pools with salinity and sea-ice context.
locator: Results and Discussion 3.1; Figs. 1-2
confidence_note: The selective enrichment is measured, while attribution to sea-ice melt is a distribution-based source inference.

subject: driver:trace-metal-availability
statement: Five-day iron additions produced little chlorophyll response in the polynya, a larger offshore response, and a highly variable sea-ice-zone response, showing that iron sensitivity differs across Amundsen hydrographic regimes.
scope: Four polynya and five each oceanic and sea-ice-zone incubation stations.
evidence_basis: Shipboard iron enrichment and chlorophyll-a ratio after five days relative to paired controls.
locator: Results and Discussion 3.1; Fig. 1d and Fig. S2
confidence_note: Chlorophyll response is directly measured, but carbon fixation, species turnover, and co-limitation were not isolated.

subject: region:ross-sea
statement: A two-year Ross Sea eDNA survey detected 92 eukaryotic species in both 2024 and 2025, including Antarctic diatoms and dinoflagellates.
scope: 101 multi-depth seawater samples across 20 stations in 2024 and 12 stations in 2025 within the Ross Sea Region MPA.
evidence_basis: Environmental-DNA marker amplification, taxonomic assignment, and cross-year detection comparison.
locator: Abstract and Results: annual comparison and species-level composition
confidence_note: Cross-year detection is clear, but eDNA does not establish organism abundance, viability, or activity.

subject: driver:water-mass
statement: Thermal stratification and water-mass properties were the leading measured correlates of vertical and horizontal Ross Sea eukaryotic community separation.
scope: Late-summer CTD-depth eDNA samples from 2024 and 2025 Ross Sea surveys.
evidence_basis: Multivariate association of eDNA community dissimilarity with hydrographic variables.
locator: Abstract and Results: environmental drivers of community structure
confidence_note: The environmental associations are strong but observational and do not demonstrate a manipulated causal response.

subject: driver:chemical-dispersant
statement: Dispersed-oil and dispersant-only ice showed early enrichment of Gammaproteobacteria, including Oleispira, Bermanella, and Pseudoalteromonas, relative to clean experimental ice.
scope: Eighty-nine-day cold-room mesocosms formed from Ofotfjorden seawater.
evidence_basis: Shotgun metagenomic community profiles, qPCR, principal response curves, and time-resolved treatment comparison.
locator: Results: Prokaryotic community structure; Figs. 3-4
confidence_note: The compositional shift is supported, but there was only one dispersant-only mesocosm and pooled sequencing libraries.

subject: habitat:sea-ice
statement: Oil- and dispersant-exposed experimental sea ice accumulated hydrocarbon-degradation gene potential, but heavy hydrocarbons showed less than 10% depletion after 89 days.
scope: Dispersed-oil, dispersant, clean-ice, and sterile-control mesocosms.
evidence_basis: HMM-based detection of hydrocarbon-degradation genes and MAG pathways paired with gas-chromatographic residual-hydrocarbon measurements.
locator: Results: oil-hydrocarbon depletion and functional profiles; Fig. 1 and supplementary gene analyses
confidence_note: Genetic potential is credible, but compound loss combines biological and physical processes and does not show that every annotated pathway was active.

subject: habitat:sea-ice-ridge
statement: MOSAiC pressure ridges contained unique communities and summer algal biomass up to eight-fold higher than level ice or surface water.
scope: Three central-Arctic ridges sampled from winter through summer and compared with level ice and seawater.
evidence_basis: Chlorophyll a, microscopy, cell abundance, 16S/18S sequencing, and habitat-resolved comparisons.
locator: Results: Habitat complexity and associated microbial communities; Figs. 3-5
confidence_note: The hotspot observations are direct for sampled ridge habitats, though ridge identity and season are partly confounded.

subject: habitat:sea-ice-ridge
statement: For a 40-square-kilometre MOSAiC area in July, ridges occupying 22% of sea-ice area were estimated to contain 80 ± 20% of area-integrated ice-associated chlorophyll a.
scope: Geometry and standing-stock scaling around the MOSAiC central observatory, not a pan-Arctic flux estimate.
evidence_basis: Observed ridge geometry, areal fraction, and July chlorophyll standing stocks scaled against first- and second-year level ice.
locator: Results: Habitat complexity and associated microbial communities; Tables 3-4
confidence_note: The local standing-stock estimate is transparent but sensitive to ridge geometry, areal fraction, sampling heterogeneity, and extrapolation.

subject: habitat:rotten-sea-ice
statement: Highly porous July rotten ice near Utqiaġvik contained prokaryotic communities distinct from earlier-season ice and vertically homogeneous within each floe.
scope: Two rotten landfast-ice floes compared with May and June ice and underlying seawater.
evidence_basis: 16S rRNA gene and transcript profiles, cell counts, and vertical physicochemical measurements.
locator: Discussion 4.1 and Conclusions
confidence_note: The habitat contrast is supported, but only two rotten floes were sampled and they differed from each other.

subject: habitat:rotten-sea-ice
statement: Despite drainage and vertical homogenization of dissolved properties, rotten ice retained particulate carbon, nitrogen, and extracellular polymeric material toward its upper horizons.
scope: Vertical profiles through two July rotten-ice floes near Utqiaġvik.
evidence_basis: Measured particulate carbon and nitrogen, extracellular polymeric substances, porosity, and vertical profiles.
locator: Discussion 4.1 and Conclusions
confidence_note: Retention was observed in the sampled floes; the magnitude and fate of release after breakup were not measured.

subject: habitat:sea-ice
statement: During a 49-hour Fram Strait melt experiment, about one-tenth of bacterial and microeukaryotic taxa in original sea ice were directly traceable in meltwater, with larger cells and aggregates contributing strongly.
scope: Short controlled melt of Fram Strait sea ice and paired seawater.
evidence_basis: Time-resolved, size-fractionated bacterial and eukaryotic amplicon sequencing.
locator: Abstract; Results: microbial signatures specific to original ice and ice melt
confidence_note: Sequence overlap establishes short-term transfer but not viability, activity, longer persistence, or in situ flux.

subject: process:sea-ice-melt-export
statement: Ten of 128 molecular formulae unique to original sea ice were subsequently detected in meltwater, providing a chemical fingerprint of ice-to-water connectivity.
scope: Forty-nine-hour Fram Strait sea-ice melt microcosm.
evidence_basis: FT-ICR-MS molecular-formula comparison among original ice, seawater, and meltwater.
locator: Results 3.4: Chemical signatures of melting sea ice
confidence_note: Formula overlap supports transfer but does not uniquely identify molecular structures, bioavailability, or ecosystem-scale flux.

subject: src:scs-haima-anme-zonation
statement: ANME lineages occupied different sediment niches: ANME-2a/b predominated in upper and middle sulfate–methane transition layers, whereas ANME-1b was more prominent in deeper sulfate-depleted layers.
scope: Haima seep core QDN-14B and non-seep core QDN-31B, northwestern South China Sea.
evidence_basis: Two piston cores compared using geochemical profiles, archaeal 16S rRNA genes, and mcrA phylogeny.
locator: Abstract
confidence_note: Two cores describe local zonation; marker-gene occurrence does not identify electron-transfer mechanisms.

subject: src:scs-gmgs2-hydrate-diversity
statement: Microbial assemblages differed among hydrate-bearing, transition, and carbonate zones; ANME-1b occurred prominently in hydrate-bearing intervals.
scope: GMGS2-08, northern South China Sea, including present and buried seep systems.
evidence_basis: qPCR and 16S rRNA sequencing compared sulfate–methane transition, carbonate, and upper/lower hydrate-bearing zones.
locator: Abstract
confidence_note: Taxonomic patterns support habitat differentiation, while the proposed AOM roles remain inferred.

subject: src:scs-water-particle-fractions
statement: Particle-attached and free-living prokaryotic fractions differed in abundance and diversity; free-living communities were more associated with temperature and inorganic nutrients.
scope: Water above two South China Sea cold seeps.
evidence_basis: Particle-attached and free-living fractions analyzed by 16S rRNA sequencing and qPCR along vertical geochemical gradients.
locator: Abstract
confidence_note: Fractions are operationally defined; amplicons do not quantify methane oxidation or organic-carbon turnover rates.

subject: src:scs-new-seep-dna-rna
statement: DNA- and RNA-derived assemblages differed, with RNA libraries showing stronger representation of methane-cycling archaea and sulfate reducers in particular seep habitats.
scope: Newly developed ROV05 and ROV07 seeps, northern South China Sea.
evidence_basis: ROV cores and surface samples across living clams, dead shells, and carbonate habitats; paired DNA/RNA amplicons, qPCR, and geochemistry.
locator: Abstract; Site Description and Sampling
confidence_note: RNA enrichment is an activity indicator, not a direct measurement of AOM rate; the associated corrigendum should accompany citation.

subject: src:scs-sulfur-smtz-genomes
statement: The 110 recovered sulfur-cycling genomes supported distinct niches above and below SMTZ, linking inferred sulfur metabolism with carbon fixation and nitrogen fixation.
scope: Eight cores from two South China Sea seep areas, including three shallow-SMTZ cores.
evidence_basis: Genome reconstruction and transcript evidence used to characterize sulfur-oxidizing and sulfur-reducing populations above and below SMTZ.
locator: Abstract
confidence_note: Genomic pathways and transcripts do not directly determine electron budgets or in situ process rates.

subject: src:scs-haima-bottom-water-intensity
statement: Bottom-water bacterial composition differed among seep-intensity regimes; the high-intensity site had the lowest alpha diversity and methane was associated with community variation.
scope: Haima non-seep, low-intensity, and high-intensity sites; water approximately 50 cm above seabed.
evidence_basis: ROV-mounted Niskin bottles; 4 L filtered through 0.22 µm membranes; 16S sequencing compared with methane, nutrients, and DOC.
locator: Abstract; Collection of Bottom-Water Samples and Geochemical Analysis
confidence_note: One expedition and correlative community analyses do not establish hydrocarbon degradation rates.

subject: src:scs-site-f-mag-resource
statement: The study supplied 768 MAGs from Site F samples, including 597 bacterial and 171 archaeal genomes, expanding genomic references across seep compartments.
scope: Site F waters, seep fluids, fluids beneath fauna, and sediment cores.
evidence_basis: 23 metagenomes; near-fauna water collected by ROV and filtered through 0.22 µm membranes, with depth-sectioned sediment cores.
locator: Abstract; Sampling; Data Records
confidence_note: MAGs ranged in completeness; the number is a recovered-genome count, not a count of viable species.

subject: src:scs-methane-supply-assembly
statement: Communities grouped by methane-supply regime across sites, with ANME-1 more prominent under high supply and ANME-2 under low supply.
scope: Eleven sediment cores from two geographically separated South China Sea seeps.
evidence_basis: Geochemical and microbiological profiles; assembly models and co-occurrence networks compared across methane-supply classes.
locator: Abstract
confidence_note: Supply classes and network models do not prove causal interactions between individual taxa.

subject: src:scs-deep-hydrate-fermentation
statement: Abundant populations carried and expressed macromolecule-fermentation pathways, while classical sulfate reducers, methanogens, and methanotrophs were comparatively rare.
scope: Qiongdongnan Basin and Shenhu hydrate sediments; analyzed samples to 49 m below seabed.
evidence_basis: Four drill cores, geochemical zonation, MAGs, and metatranscriptomes compared above and below sulfate–methane interfaces.
locator: Abstract; Sampling sites
confidence_note: Transcription supports metabolic engagement but does not quantify the energy contribution of fermentation for the entire sediment column.

subject: src:scs-seep-population-evolution
statement: Population genomes showed generally low homologous recombination and strong purifying selection, with sediment-depth-dependent diversification of key metabolic genes.
scope: Six global seep sites, including Haima, Site F, and Haiyang 4; sediments to 430 cm.
evidence_basis: Microdiversity and selection analysis for 39 abundant methane-oxidizing and sulfate-reducing species from 68 metagenomes.
locator: Abstract; Methods: Metagenomes for deep-sea cold seep sediments
confidence_note: Global aggregate results must be distinguished from SCS-specific populations; sampling and read coverage affect microdiversity recovery.

subject: src:scs-metal-dependent-aom
statement: Geochemical, omics, and model evidence supported an additional methane sink linked to iron and manganese reduction in methanic sediments.
scope: Haima core HM-S11; methanic sediments beneath the sulfate-rich zone.
evidence_basis: Porewater/solid geochemistry, DNA/RNA communities, metagenomes, metatranscriptomes, and modeling examined Fe/Mn-linked AOM.
locator: Abstract; Sampling and geochemical analyses
confidence_note: The pathway contribution is model-estimated; it does not experimentally confirm a specific metal-reducing partner.

subject: src:scs-active-aom-pathways
statement: The study provided incubation evidence for nitrate/nitrite-dependent methane oxidation in addition to sulfate-associated pathways in SCS seep sediments.
scope: Nine stations in Haima, Site F, and Xisha Trough; 0–4 cm surface sediments.
evidence_basis: Surface sediments were examined with geochemistry and 13CH4 slurry incubations under sulfate, nitrate, and nitrite amendments.
locator: Abstract; Sample collection and chemical analysis; Measurement of AOM rates
confidence_note: Incubation potentials are not equivalent to unamended in situ rates or region-wide pathway fractions.

subject: src:scs-campylobacterota-interface
statement: Culture and transcript evidence linked Campylobacterota to hydrogen utilization, sulfur transformations, and nitrate consumption at the seep interface.
scope: Formosa cold seep, seawater–sediment interface and reduced sediment.
evidence_basis: Sulfurovum/Sulfurimonas isolates integrated with comparative genomes, transcripts, geochemistry, and gas-tight in situ sampling.
locator: Abstract; Sampling and
confidence_note: Functions of cultured representatives and expressed pathways should not be assigned uniformly to all Campylobacterota.

subject: src:scs-haima-viral-evolution
statement: The study recovered 338 vOTUs and identified candidate viral persistence strategies alongside low within-population nucleotide diversity.
scope: Two active and one extinct Haima seep site; upper 18–20 cm sediments.
evidence_basis: Viral genomes, predicted hosts, defense systems, and population nucleotide diversity recovered from bulk sediment metagenomes.
locator: Abstract; Sample description, metagenomic sequencing and analysis
confidence_note: Host links and auxiliary functions are computational predictions; sequence recovery does not demonstrate active infection.

subject: src:scs-haima-fungal-networks
statement: Fungal sequences occupied connected network positions and fungal genes were transcribed in seep sediments, supporting inclusion of fungi in seep-microbiome studies.
scope: Haima seep/control sediments plus comparative datasets from ten global seep regions.
evidence_basis: 147-sample fungal/prokaryotic networks integrated with metagenomic and metatranscriptomic searches for fungal enzymes.
locator: Abstract; Environmental context of cold seep and control samples
confidence_note: Network centrality and fungal transcripts do not demonstrate direct fungal methane oxidation or causal ecosystem control.

subject: src:scs-haima-water-sediment-networks
statement: Seep and reference samples differed in elemental distribution and bacterial network structure; water and sediment assemblages were more similar at seepage stations.
scope: Haima seep and non-seep stations; water 160–200 m above seabed and 0–6 cm sediments.
evidence_basis: CTD-rosette water samples and gravity-core surface sediments compared using community and elemental analyses.
locator: Abstract; Samples Collection
confidence_note: These water samples were not taken immediately at the interface; network association does not prove sediment-to-water migration of cells.

subject: src:scs-haima-water-assembly
statement: Prokaryotic diversity and modeled assembly processes changed with depth and hydrochemistry, with Cyanobacteria prominent near the illuminated surface and Proteobacteria deeper.
scope: Vertical water profile above Haima cold seep.
evidence_basis: Depth-stratified communities compared with hydrochemistry and statistical assembly/co-occurrence models.
locator: Abstract
confidence_note: Statistical assembly classifications depend on null-model assumptions and cannot directly measure microbial interactions.

subject: src:scs-lingshui-sitef-interface
statement: Interface microbiomes differed between Lingshui and Site F, with distinct inferred methane-, nitrogen-, and sulfur-associated functional profiles.
scope: Seven interface-water samples from Site F and Lingshui seeps.
evidence_basis: ROV-collected interface water and 16S amplicons compared across seepage and fauna habitats.
locator: Abstract; Samples collection and geochemistry measurement
confidence_note: Function predictions from marker genes do not establish the rates or realized occurrence of individual AOM pathways.

subject: src:scs-haima-mercury
statement: Upper active-seep sediments contained more Hg and methylmercury than reference sediments, alongside genes associated with mercury transformations.
scope: Haima active-seep and reference-area sediment cores.
evidence_basis: Hg/MeHg concentrations and mercury isotopes integrated with microbial hgcA, merA, and merB gene analyses.
locator: Publisher abstract
confidence_note: Gene detection does not measure methylation rate; the paper's global storage extrapolation is not a direct global inventory.

subject: src:scs-haima-water-nitrogen-fixation
statement: Nitrogen fixation occurred in Haima water and increased following sulfur-containing organic-matter enrichment; Dechloromonas genomes carried nitrogen-fixation and sulfur-oxidation genes.
scope: Water column above Haima cold seep.
evidence_basis: Nitrogen-fixation rates, nifH communities, DOM amendments, and MAGs used to examine sulfur-associated diazotrophy.
locator: Abstract
confidence_note: Amendment responses measure experimental potential; co-encoded genes do not independently establish sulfur oxidation as the in situ energy source.

subject: src:scs-haima-microeukaryote-dna-rna
statement: Prokaryotes generally had lower diversity in seep sediments than reference sediments, whereas microeukaryotes showed the opposite pattern; DNA/RNA differences were larger for microeukaryotes.
scope: Haima seep, less-active seep, and non-seep sediments.
evidence_basis: ROV sediment cores; paired DNA/RNA profiling for prokaryotes and microeukaryotes with environmental and assembly analyses.
locator: Abstract; Sampling collection and measurement of environmental factors
confidence_note: RNA signatures cannot be equated directly with biomass production or organism viability.

subject: src:scs-site-f-water-metabolism
statement: The 377 MAGs supported vertical metabolic differentiation, including methanotrophic populations from bottom-interface water into deeper mesopelagic layers.
scope: Site F, roughly 1150 m water depth; surface, mesopelagic, and near-vent water.
evidence_basis: ROV interface filtration and Niskin samples at 30–1100 m; 0.22 µm filters, MAG reconstruction, and metabolic models.
locator: Abstract; Sample collection; The metabolic potential and interaction of water column microbes
confidence_note: Predicted exchanges and methane-filtration functions are genome/model inferences rather than measured methane removal fluxes.

subject: src:scs-phosphorus-lucapcycle
statement: LucaPCycle expanded phosphorus-cycling protein detection, revealing archaeal and viral genetic potential and validating selected previously unannotated phosphatases.
scope: Sixteen global seep sites, including Haima and Qiongdongnan samples.
evidence_basis: Protein-model classification integrated with genomes, transcripts, porewater chemistry, metabolomics, and enzyme validation.
locator: Abstract; Metagenomic and metatranscriptomic datasets and processing
confidence_note: Global protein-family totals are not SCS-specific counts; annotations do not establish phosphorus flux for every host.

subject: src:scs-seep-dehalogenation
statement: Reductive-dehalogenase-like genes occurred across diverse archaeal and bacterial groups, with complementary chemical and experimental evidence supporting organohalide-transforming potential.
scope: Sixteen global seep sites, including Haima, Site F, Shenhu, and other SCS sites.
evidence_basis: RdhA-like sequence classification integrated with halogen chemistry, laboratory incubations, transcripts, and metabolomics.
locator: Abstract; Metagenomic and metatranscriptomic datasets from cold seep sediments
confidence_note: RdhA-like annotation alone does not verify substrate specificity or field-scale remediation capacity.

subject: src:scs-seep-quorum-sensing
statement: Multiple signaling systems were detected across seep taxa, and representative LuxI–LuxR pairs showed activity in heterologous tests.
scope: Seventeen global seep sites including Haima, Site F, and other SCS regions.
evidence_basis: Quorum-sensing genes and transcripts compared with environmental gradients; representative LuxI–LuxR pairs tested by heterologous expression.
locator: Abstract; Metagenomic and metatranscriptomic data processing
confidence_note: Presence and experimental function of selected signaling pairs do not demonstrate regulation of every inferred biogeochemical pathway in situ.

subject: src:scs-site-f-sponge-partitioning
statement: Sponge microbiomes had distinct composition, lower diversity, and enrichment of specialized sulfur- and methane-associated bacterial groups compared with environmental microbiomes.
scope: Site F sponge-associated, seawater, and sediment microbiomes.
evidence_basis: Six sponge species and environmental metagenomes compared using taxonomic profiles, MAGs, and functional annotations.
locator: Abstract; Sample and Data Collections
confidence_note: Different collection years confound direct habitat comparisons; functional gene abundance is not metabolic efficiency.

subject: src:scs-seep-defense-systems
statement: The comparative catalog revealed extensive defense and anti-defense diversity, and selected candidate microbial systems protected against viral infection in laboratory assays.
scope: Seventeen global seep sites; SCS sequences contribute to the comparative catalog.
evidence_basis: Microbial defense and viral anti-defense genes compared across genomes; selected candidate defenses experimentally tested.
locator: Abstract; Methods: Metagenomic datasets
confidence_note: Laboratory validation covers selected systems; co-occurrence does not establish synergism or infection rates in seep sediment.

subject: src:scs-site-f-water-spatial-2026
statement: Near-seep and deeper-water communities showed greater representation of methane- and sulfur-associated populations and genes, indicating spatially structured metabolic potential.
scope: Site F, near-seep sites and a station approximately 1 km away.
evidence_basis: Niskin bottles on CTD and ROV; 16S and metagenomic profiles compared across depth and distance.
locator: Abstract; Water Samples Collection and Pretreatment
confidence_note: Gene distributions do not quantify the fraction of vented methane removed during upward transport.

subject: src:scs-haima-domains-water-sediment-2026
statement: Microbial diversity and co-occurrence varied by compartment and habitat; modeled environmental selection differed between prokaryotes and microeukaryotes in water versus sediment.
scope: Haima water layers and mussel, anemone, bare seabed, dead-clam, and clam sediment habitats.
evidence_basis: CTD water profiles and ROV sediment cores to 30 cm; prokaryotic/microeukaryotic community and co-occurrence analyses.
locator: Abstract; Sample collection and measurement of environmental factors
confidence_note: Correlations and assembly models indicate ecological patterns, not demonstrated interspecies exchanges.

subject: src:scs-seep-nitrogen-methane-n2o
statement: Nitrate/nitrite-coupled methane oxidation had a larger potential contribution in early-stage than mature seep sediments, and nitrate/methane amendments increased net N2O production.
scope: Early-stage and mature South China Sea seep sediments.
evidence_basis: 14C labeling, omics, and gas-production analyses tested nitrate/nitrite-linked methane oxidation and N2O formation.
locator: Abstract; Sample collection and geochemical analysis
confidence_note: Potential rates and amendment responses cannot be treated as continuous natural emissions or global climate offsets.

subject: src:scs-newborn-seep-biofilter
statement: A methane-consuming animal–microbe assemblage developed within approximately one to two years at the monitored newborn seep, with aerobic and anaerobic methanotrophs and bioturbating fauna.
scope: Human-induced newborn SCS seep compared with mature seeps and slope references.
evidence_basis: More than 40 sites around the discharge center; ROV cores, porewater, molecular analyses, and in situ ecosystem observations.
locator: Abstract; Sediment and porewater sampling
confidence_note: One induced seep does not establish a universal recovery time or guaranteed mitigation of future methane releases.

subject: src:scs-haima-anme1-hotspots
statement: ANME-1 genomes contained variable hotspots associated with defense, transport, and methane-metabolism genes; heterologous hicAB tests supported toxin–antitoxin function.
scope: Haima sediment core at 1435 m water depth; four depth intervals within 30 cm.
evidence_basis: Long-read reconstruction of circular MAGs, genomic-hotspot comparisons, and heterologous tests of hicAB operons.
locator: Abstract; Sampling, DNA extraction, metagenomic library preparations and sequencing
confidence_note: One core and heterologous assays do not prove the drivers of speciation or stress responses in natural ANME populations.

subject: src:scs-haima-clam-sulfide-2026
statement: Moderate sulfide shortage preserved symbiont abundance, whereas severe shortage coincided with reduced abundance and altered host lysosomal pathways; sulfur-metabolism responses indicated symbiotic flexibility.
scope: Archivesica marissinica and sulfur-oxidizing symbionts at Haima, including HM-2 and HM-3.
evidence_basis: In situ clam transplantation with host/symbiont molecular profiling under moderate and severe sulfide shortage.
locator: Abstract
confidence_note: Molecular associations support a proposed buffering mechanism but do not directly measure symbiont carbon transfer or long-term resilience.

subject: src:scs-site-f-sponge-host-specificity
statement: The six sponge species hosted distinct bacterial assemblages, with SUP05 prominent in most samples.
scope: Six sponge species at the Formosa Ridge cold seep.
evidence_basis: Sixteen sponge samples analyzed with full-length 16S amplicons and bacterial phylogeny.
locator: Abstract; 2.1 Sample collection; 2.3 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing and processing
confidence_note: Marker phylogeny does not measure sulfur/methane oxidation or establish the mechanism of host specificity.
